players.product: data-center chillers, BASX custom air handlers & liquid-cooling packages (Redmond / Memphis)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO): net sales increased 42.5% year over year to $424.2 million, driven primarily by 138.8% growth in BASX-branded sales on data center cooling demand and higher Memphis utilization; AAON-branded sales rose 9.5%. Gross margin was 25.9% (vs 26.1%), pressured by unabsorbed fixed costs at the new Memphis facility; adjusted EBITDA margin 15.2%; diluted EPS $0.39.
quarterly_data.figure: net sales $424.2 million (+42.5% YoY); BASX-branded sales +138.8%; gross margin 25.9%; adj. EBITDA margin 15.2%; diluted EPS $0.39

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the data center market is AAON's most robust growth opportunity. In 2025 BASX-branded sales increased 143% to $548 million with a book-to-bill of 2.4 for the BASX brand on the year; in Q4 BASX-branded bookings again reached record levels, driving BASX backlog up 45% sequentially. Custom air and liquid cooling solutions are gaining momentum as AI data center customers require highly engineered systems.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 BASX-branded sales +143% to $548 million; book-to-bill 2.4; Q4 BASX backlog +45% sequentially

quarterly_data.signal: Segment detail (CFO/CEO): AAON Coil Products (Longview) sales increased $49.6 million, or 93.6%, driven by $75.3 million in BASX-branded liquid cooling product sales, which grew 100%. BASX segment sales grew 109.1% to $106.1 million at a 27.1% gross margin, helped by accelerated production at Memphis. Memphis achieved profitability for the first time in a quarter but still carried $6.4 million of incremental overhead in AAON Oklahoma; CEO estimates Memphis contributed around $25 million to $30 million in Q4.
quarterly_data.figure: Coil Products +$49.6 million (+93.6%); BASX liquid cooling sales $75.3 million (+100%); BASX segment $106.1 million (+109.1%), GM 27.1%; Memphis ~$25 million to $30 million in Q4

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook: sales growth of 18% to 20%, gross margin of 29% to 31% with uneven quarterly progression as capacity ramps, SG&A about 16% of sales, D&A of $95 million to $100 million. CEO: BASX growth built into the guide is about half of the 50% range an analyst asked about, with much of the growth coming from the AAON brand in Tulsa; the year starts softer and strengthens through the year.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 sales growth 18% to 20%; gross margin 29% to 31%; SG&A about 16%; D&A $95 million to $100 million

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on why BASX backlog converts slowly: data center customers do not buy on a lead-time basis; the backlog is built on longer-duration, multi-phase projects and programs, giving ramp clarity into 2026 and 2027. Some backlog may move in or out as the whole data center supply network feels the pressure of overall demand on project deliveries.

Capacity (CEO): after the Longview expansion and Memphis facility, the team aims to unlock more than the $1.5 billion footprint capacity previously discussed within the existing investment before another substantial capital step-up; mapping that opportunity in early 2026. Near term, square footage does not limit new BASX orders; the ramp rate is the limiting factor. Manufacturing footprint expanded by more than 25% over the past eighteen months.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $1.5 billion BASX footprint capacity targeted; footprint expanded more than 25%

quarterly_data.signal: Liquid cooling mix (CEO, responding to an analyst's 37.8% liquid-cooling share figure): liquid cooling revenue is driven primarily through the Longview plant for BASX; as Memphis adds a broader portfolio including high-performance pre-cooling chiller products, the liquid cooling percentage may moderate a little, but total liquid cooling dollars are expected to keep growing. AAON targets high-performance liquid cooling opportunities tied to customer platform development rather than lower-capacity, high-volume, lower-margin orders.

BASX customer mix (CEO): single large data center orders can skew a quarter's customer concentration, but bookings show new customers and growing diversity across hyperscalers, build-to-suit colocation providers and colocation providers. BASX secured a strong volume of new orders at attractive margins in Q4, with the majority scheduled for production at Memphis.
